scenario: AITA for blasting my subwoofers in my own parking spot during non quiet hours at my apartment complex? | Posting from a throwaway for whatever reason, just don't want this to blend into my other subs. So basically my car is my life. I have a tuned Subaru Impreza WRX STI that is my hobby, my transportation, my life, I'm more comfortable behind the wheel than I am in my own bed. Its not quite as fast as I want it but it looks amazing and the sound system is seriously as good as it can be. I live in a large apartment complex in Tucson, I'm guessing probably 100 units or so. Not sure. Anyways the complex is really cool because a lot of places won't let you work on your car, well I can pay an extra premium every month to get a mechanics spot under shade. It's an extra 2 bills a month but so worth it. When I work on my car I BLAST my system. It helps me think and focus. Also important to note our complex has quiet hours between and 10pm and 8am, I follow these to the letter but I do need to work on my car so some Saturday's and Sunday's I crank shit from 8:01am to 9:59pm. I am not breaking any rules at all. I moved in in January and this Sunday was apparently a major problem. I had two people ask me to turn it down. I totally did but one came back and said its not the volume, it's the bass, can I turn the bass down. I said I would try but I guess that wasn't good enough because he came down a third time. Finally I told him I paid for the spot, I wasn't breaking any rules, I'd only be out there until 10pm. He said his kids had to go to bed at 8:30 and the bass from my car was rattling his walls. I told him I'd done my best to accommodate him but I was done. He told me he'd call the police (who never showed) and talk to management. I just stopped responding to him and cranked my system to drown our his barking. I worked on my car until 9:59 when I turned my system off. I got an email from my apartment manager asking if she could come by. She's really cool and I want to help her but I feel like I'm paying extra for the mechanics spot, I'm not breaking any rules and that guy had no right to talk to me like that. She said she managed a nice place and she's gotten complaint after complaint about my car. I told her I was sorry but I was still well within my rights and not breaking rules. She asked me to please consider for her sake using headphones Or earbuds if music is that important to me. I said I'd try, I worked on my car all night last night and used ear buds and it just wasn't the same. I spent thousands of dollars and so much time to tune my system perfectly and to not use it when I want sucks. I want to help her out but am I even being an asshole in the first place?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand all the details.

The person is a woman who has a Subaru that's her passion. She's into car audio and has a really good sound system. She lives in an apartment complex that allows her to pay extra for a mechanics spot to work on her car. The complex has quiet hours from 10pm to 8am, which she follows strictly. On weekends, she works on her car from 8:01am to 9:59pm, blasting her music. She says she's not breaking any rules.

One Sunday, two people asked her to turn it down. She complied with the first request, but the second person came back saying it's the bass that's the problem. She tried to adjust it, but the person came back a third time. She told him she's within her rights and would stop at 10pm. He threatened to call the police and talk to management. She ignored him, turned her system up, and worked until 9:59pm. She then got an email from her manager, who is nice, but has received complaints. The manager asked her to use headphones or earbuds. She tried, but it wasn't the same experience, so she didn't use them all night.

Now, she's wondering if she's being an asshole.

So, the question is: Is it morally acceptable for her to blast her subwoofers during non-quiet hours, even if it's causing disturbances to her neighbors?

First, I need to consider the rules of the apartment complex. She's following the quiet hours, so she's not breaking any rules in that sense. However, the issue is that her music, especially the bass, is disturbing her neighbors, even during non-quiet hours.

Morally, the key points are respecting others' peace and comfort, even if you're within the rules. Just because something is allowed doesn't mean it's considerate. She's causing a disturbance that's affecting her neighbors' ability to have a quiet environment, especially for their children who have to go to bed early.

She did try to accommodate by turning the volume down and adjusting the bass, but it wasn't enough. When the neighbor came back a third time, she became confrontational and turned the music up, which is not a good response. It shows a lack of willingness to compromise and consider others' feelings.

Additionally, when the manager asked her to use headphones, she tried but didn't stick with it because it wasn't the same experience. This indicates that her priority is her own enjoyment over the comfort of her neighbors.

So, even though she's not breaking any rules, her actions are causing unnecessary disturbances. Morally, it's not acceptable to ignore the impact on others, especially when there are alternative solutions available, like using headphones.

Therefore, the action is morally unacceptable.
